beats.narration_text: ECIS extracts guidance signals from earnings calls using four readers weighted by a five-dimension triangulator. A six-model ensemble predicts guidance revisions, with conformal prediction intervals, Monte Carlo dropout, and ensemble disagreement quantifying uncertainty around every forecast. The system abstains when confidence is low, tracks language shifts propagating across sectors and supply chains, and answers natural language queries through an agentic layer. This week, the system learns to see time — not just single quarters, but patterns unfolding across them.

props.sparkLine: This week: it learns to see time.

beats.narration_text: Tree-based models see each quarter as an isolated snapshot — a flat row of features with no memory of what came before. An LSTM changes that. It unrolls across four to eight quarters per company, passing a hidden state forward through time. A gradual hedging ramp over four quarters is a different signal than a single-quarter spike, and the LSTM learns the difference from sequence structure alone. A lighter GRU variant trains thirty percent faster with comparable accuracy. Both now sit alongside the tree models — sequence-aware predictions complementing snapshot-based ones.

The same hedging increase means something different in a bull market than in a bear market. A Hidden Markov Model now detects three market regimes — bullish, bearish, and transitional — fitted on sector-level signal aggregates using the Baum-Welch algorithm. Each quarter gets a regime label, and that label feeds into every prediction model as a context feature. The models can now adjust their behavior depending on the broader market environment instead of treating all quarters the same.

props.sparkLine: The same signal, a different market.

beats.narration_text: Not all analyst questions are equal. The system now profiles individual analysts — tracking their question types, difficulty levels, and how closely their framing aligns with management responses. This matters for dodge scoring. Dodging a hard question from a known tough analyst is less informative than dodging a routine question from a friendly one. The raw dodge score might be identical, but once you normalize for analyst difficulty, the signal diverges. The same evasion, weighted by who asked, tells a different story.

props.sparkLine: The same evasion, a different asker.

beats.narration_text: The agentic layer can now read the transcripts directly. Retrieval-augmented generation connects the agent to both the transcript corpus in ChromaDB and the structured signal database in PostgreSQL. A single query — why was Company A flagged — triggers semantic search over raw transcripts for the exact language that triggered the signal, and a structured query for the metrics behind it. The agent synthesizes both into one response: the quote and the number, side by side.

props.sparkLine: The quote and the number, together.

beats.narration_text: Twenty phases in, the system sees time through LSTM and GRU sequence models, reads the market environment through regime detection, understands who is asking the questions through analyst profiling, and can cite the actual transcripts when explaining its reasoning. Every layer of context — temporal, environmental, interpersonal — makes the signal more precise. The system doesn't just extract what was said. It remembers what was said before. Next week, we keep building.

Let's recap with Claude. Every model in this system until now saw a quarter as a row — a snapshot with no memory of the one before it. Sequence models change that: the same hedging level reached gradually over a year means something different from the same level reached in one jump, and the model can finally tell those apart. Regime detection adds the second kind of context, because a signal in a bull market is not the same signal in a bear one. Analyst profiling adds the third, which is the one most systems never get to: the same evasion means more or less depending on who asked the question. And the agent can now quote the transcript it drew the conclusion from, rather than just reporting the number.
